trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Host value may become the authority of absolute URLs generated by the application. At the pinned commit the decision is implicit trust in StandardRequestUriProvider.getHost(), which accepts any syntactically valid header value; the published fix moves the decision into a Jetty HttpConfiguration customizer that compares the header against nifi.web.proxy.host for secure requests.

landing_point.why: The summary says qualified URLs are built from proxy host headers; this is the only place the application resolves a host from X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Host for URL construction, and it performs no allow-list check.

fix_sites.entry_point: Every HTTPS request through the NiFi web connector (UI, /nifi-api REST, OIDC/SAML callbacks, content viewers); the parsed allow-list is built from nifi.web.proxy.host via NiFiProperties.getAllowedHostsAsList()
Every HTTPS request through the NiFi web connector; registered at fix.diff:89-90 as an HttpConfiguration.Customizer that throws HTTP 421 on unlisted proxy host headers

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the pinned documentation scope nifi.web.proxy.host to the Host header of secure (HTTPS) requests, so a solver can argue the plain-HTTP path and the separate NiFi Registry product (which has no proxy host property at all) were never covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Proxy host headers that carry an explicit port (X-ProxyHost: nifi.apache.org:8443) and headers whose value equals the request's own host are legitimate: the sink deliberately parses host and port out of the proxy host header. A blanket reject of any value not exactly in the allow-list (which the published getValidProxyHosts builds by splitting the configured value on every colon) breaks that shape and any IPv6 bracket form.

O6_input_shapes: bare domain name configured in nifi.web.proxy.host (e.g. nifi.apache.org)
domain:port configured in nifi.web.proxy.host, port stripped by HOST_PORT_SEPARATOR.split (fix.diff:104-106)
both X-ProxyHost and X-Forwarded-Host present on one request; each is validated independently (fix.diff:192-207)
proxy host header value equal to the request URI host, exempted via requestHost.equals (fix.diff:199)
absent proxy host header skipped; empty/blank header values are still validated and therefore rejected

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plain-HTTP deployment: a request through a TLS-terminating proxy reaches NiFi on nifi.web.http.port, so request.isSecure() is false, the new customizer returns the request unchanged, and StandardRequestUriProvider still honours an arbitrary X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Host when building absolute URLs.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The pinned documentation says the property and Host matching apply only when NiFi runs securely, so the HTTP path reads as out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: The sink is in nifi-commons/nifi-web-servlet-shared; the guard that skips it lives in nifi-framework-bundle/.../nifi-jetty (different module, different bundle).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: X-ProxyPort / X-Forwarded-Port are still consumed with no allow-list, so a qualified URL can be built with an arbitrary port even when the host itself is validated.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory and the property text talk about the host; the Host/authority port is already covered by HostPortValidatorCustomizer, so the proxy port reads as a separate, already-handled concern.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same class as the landing point; the analogous guard lives in nifi-jetty (HostPortValidatorCustomizer) one module away.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Registry-side ProxyHeaderValidatorCustomizer added to the Registry HttpConfiguration, mirroring the framework one.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Registry connector factory already extends the same StandardServerConnectorFactory and already overrides getHttpConfiguration to add header size settings; the framework fix is a direct copy-paste away.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A host-header validator alongside the existing proxy context path validator at the Jetty handler layer.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This class already reads proxy headers at the Jetty layer and already enforces an allow-list (for context paths), so a maintainer adding host enforcement here is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A sibling parser of nifi.web.proxy.host with its own regex, used to derive certificate subject alternative names.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The property is already parsed in a second place with a different rule set; a maintainer hardening the allow-list would plausibly also correct or reuse this parser.

O9_family: Origin validation error / host header injection into generated absolute URLs (CWE-346)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module reactor with ./mvnw, JDK 21 (maven.compiler.release=21), version 2.10.0-SNAPSHOT
O10_build.project_tests: nifi-framework-bundle/nifi-framework/nifi-web/nifi-jetty StandardServerProviderTest starts an in-process Jetty HTTPS server with an ephemeral keystore and asserts 302/421/400 for Host and proxy host headers; nifi-commons/nifi-web-servlet-shared StandardRequestUriProviderTest and RequestUriBuilderTest cover header-to-URI mapping.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a host allow-list check inside StandardRequestUriProvider.getHost (or a servlet Filter in front of the REST API), which leaves the Jetty-level path, the plain-HTTP connector mode and the port route open.

out_of_scope_notes: NiFi Registry (same repository, separate product) builds its base URI from X-ProxyHost / X-Forwarded-Server with no allow-list and has no proxy host property (nifi-registry/nifi-registry-core/nifi-registry-properties/.../NiFiRegistryProperties.java has no matching key); recorded as O2 and not pursued further.

Registry's Jetty redirect rule is constructed with an empty allowed context path list with the comment 'Can be extended with property support' (nifi-registry/nifi-registry-core/nifi-registry-jetty/src/main/java/org/apache/nifi/registry/jetty/JettyServer.java:95) - outside this advisory.

DataTransferResource derives its transfer URL from req.getRequestURL() rather than proxy headers (nifi-framework-bundle/nifi-framework/nifi-web/nifi-web-api/src/main/java/org/apache/nifi/web/api/DataTransferResource.java:306) - different mechanism, not pursued.
